claims.text: Failure modes (external calls): `cma pseudonymise` makes no network call; the only external input it reads besides the statement is firm_rules.yaml, and a malformed one is refused with exit 2, naming the file and quoting no description text, and no folder is created at --out. New test: test_cli_a_malformed_firm_rules_file_is_refused_and_nothing_is_written (contracts).

claims.text: Failure modes (idempotency): the same input gives byte-identical output and profile, and a second run to the same --out refuses (exit 2) rather than overwriting.

Failure modes (partial failure): the files are written into a staging folder and renamed into place, so a write that fails part-way (ENOSPC on the second file) leaves no partial copy and no staging folder, and the next run starts clean.
Failure modes (retries/backoff/dead letter): not applicable. This is a one-shot local command with no queue and no retried call.

Data/PII: names and account numbers in the description and in every other column the loader accepts (payee, account_number, reference) become consistent tokens. Ids, dates, amounts and balances are kept. A header with spaces around its names is read as the loader reads it. The token mapping is never written, and the output files are 0600 inside a 0700 folder.

claims.text: P10 (invariants): the copy gives the original's line categories, figures, buckets, monthly cells and indicators under v1 and v2, across every synthetic archetype × risk profile, plain and with all features. Since attempt 3 this includes the firm's own rules, with which the CLI checks the copy (firm_rules.for_case()), so a counterparty a firm rule names is kept and categorised identically.

Security (input validation and output safety): the input statement goes through contract.checked (the loader) before anything is written. Every rewritten cell is passed through contract.neutralise_formula, and the test asserts that a =HYPERLINK cell no longer starts with '='. A refusal names lines and figures and never quotes description text.

claims.text: Performance: measured, not optimised. pseudonymise_statement takes about 3.3s on 285 synthetic lines, 3.1s on 1,096, and 24.5s on a 10,000-line statement (5,911 words replaced). The cost is dominated by the P10 self-check, which recomputes everything under both rulesets, and by scanning every v1/v2 rule per cell. No query, list endpoint or pagination is involved.

dispositions.finding: major: only the description column is pseudonymised; extra columns (payee, account number) are copied verbatim (pseudonymise.py:332, 366-379)
dispositions.evidence: At 4c2999d, _rows treats every column outside id/date/amount/balance as a cell to pseudonymise. test_p10_every_column_beyond_the_five_is_pseudonymised (payee, account_number and reference columns holding JANE DOE and 12345678) passes, and neither value survives.

dispositions.finding: a header with spaces around column names crashes the pseudonymiser with KeyError (pseudonymise.py:233)
dispositions.evidence: _rows now strips header names, as the loader does. test_a_header_with_spaces_around_its_names_is_pseudonymised passes through both the library and the CLI (exit 0).

dispositions.finding: major: firm rules ignored; _kept_spans keeps no firm-rule wording and figures() categorises without firm rules, so P10 fails for a firm with firm rules (pseudonymise.py:397)
dispositions.evidence: The CLI passes firm_rules.for_case().rules. _kept_spans keeps firm-rule spans, and figures()/differs() categorise with them. test_p10_the_firms_own_rules_categorise_the_copy_as_the_original passes: ACME TRUST is kept, SMITH is tokenised, figures are equal under v1 and v2, and the line's rule is firm:acme_trust.

notes: Gaps that need the owner (no code change, to stay in scope): (1) Observability: no case-log or structured log event records that a pseudonymised copy was made. Whether making a copy should be audited in the source case's log, when --profile names a case, is a design call (R43 lists the case-log writers and T39 is not among them). (2) Performance: 10,000 lines take about 24.5s, most of it the two-ruleset P10 self-check. No requirement sets a target for this command (R52's 2s target is for the workspace recompute); if one is wanted, the self-check and the per-cell scan of every rule are where the time goes. (3) No CHANGELOG exists in the repo. (4) Library callers of pseudonymise_statement get firm_rules=() by default, so only the CLI applies the firm's rules; a future caller (for example the workspace) must pass firm_rules.for_case().rules or P10 will not hold for firms with firm rules.
